epic.intent:
Dark Mechanicus replaces the markdown `/board` workflow that this repository and the person's other repositories (for example CapitalGains and AI-DND-Matrix) were planned with. That workflow keeps `board/backlog|in-progress|done/`, with `NNN-*.md` epics and `NNN.M-*.md` sub-tickets that have checkbox acceptance criteria, driven by the `complete-ticket`, `collapse-epic` and `delivery-standards` agent skills.

**Outcomes**
1. **Agent-ready setup.** Setting up a repository can also connect Claude Code. Setup writes a project `.mcp.json` entry that launches the installed app's MCP server for that repository, merged with any servers already in the file, next to the existing "install skills" step.
2. **Migration for board-style repositories.** When a repository being set up has an old-style `/board`, Dark Mechanicus detects it, previews its open epics and tickets, imports them as Dark Mechanicus epics on confirmation, and offers to remove the old board workflow files. Nothing is deleted without the person's confirmation, and nothing is committed.
3. **Dogfood on this repository.** Retire this repository's `board/`, its board-driving skills (in `.claude/skills/` and `.cursor/skills/`), the Cursor rule, and the board sections of the README, `.ai-instructions.md` and docs. Keep the engineering standards (TDD-first, lint, tests, fireguard, deadcode, build) in a board-free form that points at Dark Mechanicus tickets.

**Context:** the hand-written `.mcp.json` at the repository root (planner role, `--allow-save`, absolute macOS paths) is the reference for what setup should generate. The board's only open work (014.3 and 014.4) has already moved into the Dark Mechanicus epic "Cross-host validation and release".

**Out of scope:** importing completed board epics as Dark Mechanicus run history (Git history keeps them); config files for agent hosts other than Claude Code (the copy-paste snippet still covers them); changing MCP roles or the tool surface.

successCriteria.text: From the desktop setup flow, a person can write a Dark Mechanicus server entry into the repository's `.mcp.json`. Other servers in the file are preserved, and an existing `darkmechanicus` entry is replaced only after confirmation.
A new Claude Code session opened in a repository set up this way lists the Dark Mechanicus tools without anyone hand-editing config (apart from the host's own one-time approval).

Setting up a repository that has an old-style `/board` shows a preview of its open epics and tickets. On confirmation, they become Dark Mechanicus epics, with titles, bodies and acceptance criteria preserved.
Removing the old board workflow files is a separate, confirmed step that lists exactly which files will be deleted. Nothing is committed.

This repository has no `board/` directory, no `complete-ticket` or `collapse-epic` skills, and no `/board` instructions in the README, `.ai-instructions.md`, the Cursor rule, the docs or the delivery standards. The delivery standards still require TDD, lint, tests, fireguard, deadcode and build.
`npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run fireguard`, `npm run deadcode`, `npm run build` and `npm run smoke:mcp` pass.

epic.title: Make Dark Mechanicus the planning system: agent-ready setup and /board retirement

bundle.rationale:
**Shape.** Sprint 1 runs four independent tickets in parallel: rewrite the standards, prune this repository's board, write `.mcp.json` from setup, and parse old boards. The riskiest new code (config merging, parsing) starts early. Sprint 2 builds the import and legacy-removal flow on top, then verifies everything.

**Critical path:** parse the board, or write .mcp.json from setup → import during setup → remove legacy files → verify.

**Why the importer waits for the .mcp.json ticket:** both change the onboarding screen and the desktop handlers. Running them in sequence avoids a three-way conflict, and the verification ticket handles the rest.

**Assumptions:**
- The person's other repositories (CapitalGains, AI-DND-Matrix) use the same board format as this repository's history, so fixtures from commit 52d6a0c are representative.
- Only open board work is imported. Done epics stay in Git history.
- Generated `.mcp.json` defaults to the planner role with `--allow-save`, matching this repository's hand-written file. Execution sessions can add an orchestrator entry later.
- `.mcp.json` contains this machine's absolute app path. Setup says so, and the person decides whether to commit it.
- This repository's open board work was moved to the "Cross-host validation and release" epic by the planner before this epic was created.

tickets.body:
Make "connect Claude Code" part of setting up a repository, so nobody has to hand-write `.mcp.json` again.

**Core (TDD first):** a pure function that merges a `darkmechanicus` server entry into the text of an existing `.mcp.json`, or creates the file.
- Preserve every other server and any unknown top-level keys.
- If the file is not valid JSON, return a clear error and leave the file untouched.
- If a `darkmechanicus` entry already exists and differs, report it, and replace it only when the caller says so.
- Build the command, args and env from `buildMcpConfig` (`src/main/desktop/mcpConfig.ts`), which already handles packaged and dev builds. Add `--role` (default `planner`) and an optional `--allow-save` (default on, matching this repository's hand-written `.mcp.json`).

**Main and IPC:** a desktop handler that writes the merged file at the repository root. Use the same path safety as `skillInstall.ts`: resolve real paths, stay inside the repository, never follow a symlink out. Never commit.

**Renderer:**
- In the MCP card on the folder home (`home/McpCard.tsx`), add a "Connect Claude Code" action next to "Install skills". Show the target path, the role, and whether save is allowed, plus a confirmation when it would replace an existing entry.
- On the onboarding screen, add an option, on by default, to also write `.mcp.json` when initializing.
- Say plainly that the file contains this machine's app path.

**Docs:** add a "Write it from the app" section to `docs/runbooks/mcp-setup.md`.

**Out of scope:** config formats for other agent hosts (the copy-paste snippet stays); the board import.

reasoning.rationale: Merges user-owned config across the core, IPC and renderer layers with file-safety rules.

tickets.body:
Use the board parser when setting up a repository that has a `board/` directory.

- **Detect:** at onboarding and on the folder home of an initialized repository, notice an old-style `board/` (`src/core/repo/discovery.ts` is a likely home).
- **Preview:** list the open epics (in-progress and backlog) with their ticket counts. List done epics as "left in Git history, not imported", and list skipped files with their reasons.
- **Import:** on confirmation, create each open epic in Backlog with its plan as a **draft**, so the person reviews and presses Save. Record the source file path in the epic intent. Re-running the import must not duplicate an epic that was already imported from the same source path.
- Implement the import as a core command so the desktop app and MCP share it. If its capability is `epic.create`, planner and orchestrator sessions get it as a tool automatically.

**Out of scope:** deleting board files (separate ticket); importing done epics as run history.

reasoning.rationale: Adds a new core command with idempotency, wired through IPC and the UI.

expectedArtifacts: Onboarding and folder-home import preview UI

tickets.body:
After a board import, offer to remove the old workflow files, as a separate confirmed step.

- **Candidates:** `board/`; the skills `complete-ticket` and `collapse-epic` under `.claude/skills/` and `.cursor/skills/`. Recognize them by directory name and by content that refers to `/board`.
- Show the exact list of paths before anything is deleted. Delete only those paths, only inside the repository, and never through a symlink. Never commit.
- Files that mention `/board` but are not safe to delete automatically (README, `.ai-instructions.md`, `delivery-standards` skills or rules) are listed as "still mentions the board, edit by hand", not deleted.
- Write tests for the candidate detection and the path safety first.

**Out of scope:** rewriting other repositories' READMEs or standards.

reasoning.rationale: Deletes user files, so detection and path safety must be exact and tested.

expectedArtifacts: Legacy-file detection and removal with tests

tickets.body:
Bring the branches together on the epic branch and prove every success criterion.

1. Merge the tickets' commits and resolve conflicts. The onboarding screen, `McpCard` and the desktop handlers are touched by several tickets.
2. **Setup with a board:** create a scratch checkout of this repository at `52d6a0c` (for example `git worktree add /tmp/dm-board-fixture 52d6a0c`). Track and set it up in the desktop app: write `.mcp.json`, import the board, and remove the legacy files. Screenshot each step.
3. **Claude Code:** open a new Claude Code session in that scratch repository, approve the project MCP server, and show that the Dark Mechanicus tools are listed (`get_capabilities` output).
4. Compare the `.mcp.json` the app generates for this repository with the hand-written one, and replace the hand-written file if it differs only in ordering or formatting.
5. Run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run fireguard`, `npm run deadcode`, `npm run build` and `npm run smoke:mcp`.
6. Report evidence for s1 to s6.

reasoning.rationale: Integrates parallel branches and verifies the full flow in the real app and agent host.
